facts.text: The first computer bug was an actual bug! In 1947, engineers found a moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer.
The first computer was called ENIAC and weighed 30 tons! It was built in 1946 and took up an entire room.
The first computer mouse was made of wood! Douglas Engelbart invented it in 1964, and it had two wheels instead of a ball.
The word 'computer' originally meant a person who did calculations by hand! It wasn't until the 1940s that it meant a machine.
The first video game was created in 1958! It was called 'Tennis for Two' and was played on an oscilloscope screen.
The first email was sent in 1971! Ray Tomlinson sent it to himself as a test, and he can't remember what it said!
The first website is still online! It was created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991 and you can still visit it at info.cern.ch.
The first computer programmer was a woman! Ada Lovelace wrote the first computer program in 1843, over 100 years before computers existed!
The first computer virus was created in 1983! It was called 'Elk Cloner' and spread through floppy disks.
The first smartphone was created in 1992! IBM's Simon Personal Communicator had a touchscreen and could send emails.
The first computer to beat a world chess champion was Deep Blue in 1997! It defeated Garry Kasparov in a 6-game match.
The first computer animation was created in 1963! It was a simple wireframe animation of a spinning cube.
The first computer with a graphical user interface (GUI) was the Xerox Alto in 1973! It had windows, icons, and a mouse.
The first computer game with graphics was Spacewar! It was created in 1962 at MIT and featured two spaceships fighting.
The first computer to use transistors was the TX-0 in 1956! Transistors made computers much smaller and faster.
The first computer to use integrated circuits was the Apollo Guidance Computer in 1966! It helped land humans on the moon.
The first personal computer was the Altair 8800 in 1975! It came as a kit that you had to build yourself.
The first laptop computer was the Osborne 1 in 1981! It weighed 24 pounds and cost $1,795.
The first computer to use a hard drive was the IBM 305 RAMAC in 1956! The hard drive was the size of two refrigerators!
The first computer to use a microprocessor was the Intel 4004 in 1971! It had 2,300 transistors and could do 60,000 calculations per second.
The first computer to use RAM (Random Access Memory) was the Manchester Baby in 1948! It had only 1,024 bits of memory.
The first computer to use a monitor was the Whirlwind in 1950! It displayed information on a cathode ray tube screen.
The first computer to use a keyboard was the UNIVAC in 1951! Before that, computers used punch cards for input.
The first computer to use a printer was the UNIVAC in 1951! It could print 600 lines per minute.
The first computer to use a floppy disk was the IBM 3740 in 1971! The floppy disk was 8 inches wide and could store 80 kilobytes.
The first computer to use a CD-ROM was the CD-i in 1991! It could store 650 megabytes of data.
The first computer to use a USB port was the iMac in 1998! USB made it easy to connect devices like keyboards and mice.
The first computer to use Wi-Fi was the iBook in 1999! It could connect to the internet wirelessly.
The first computer to use a touchscreen was the HP-150 in 1983! It had an infrared touchscreen that could detect your finger.
The first computer to use voice recognition was the IBM Shoebox in 1962! It could recognize 16 words spoken in English.
The first computer to use artificial intelligence was the Logic Theorist in 1956! It could prove mathematical theorems.
The first computer to use a webcam was the XCoffee machine in 1991! It showed a live video of a coffee pot at Cambridge University.
The first computer to use a graphics card was the IBM Professional Graphics Controller in 1984! It could display 256 colors at 640x480 resolution.
The first computer to use a sound card was the AdLib in 1987! It could play music and sound effects in games.
The first computer to use a modem was the Bell 103 in 1962! It could send data over phone lines at 300 bits per second.
